Day, night and weather

A full day and night lasts 20 real minutes. Weather in a world follows the same 30-minute pattern, so you can plan around rain and storms. Nothing skips the night: the sun keeps moving, and you cannot sleep through it.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 4 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides
Contents
  1. Day and night
  2. Weather
  3. Hold the time or weather in creative
  4. Planned, not in the game yet
  5. How this was checked

Day and night

One day and night lasts 20 real minutes. The sun is up for about 10 minutes and down for about 10. New worlds start about a minute after sunrise. Day and night

  • Night is darker and the moon is out. On clear nights you also see stars and the Milky Way; cloud hides them. Nothing dangerous happens at night because of the time of day.
  • Cows, sheep, pigs and chickens stop wandering and rest on dry ground from about a minute after sunset until about a minute before sunrise. An animal you hit still runs.
  • You cannot sleep or skip the night. Lying in a bed does not pass time (Storage, beds and lamps), and Rest / set respawn at your Home crate only sets your respawn point and refills stamina.
  • Birds sing near trees from sunrise until about midday. Night wildlife sounds take over after dark. Both are quieter in rain and silent under a roof, high above the ground, on coasts and in deserts, snowy or volcanic land.
  • In a single-player world, time stops while the pause menu, Settings or the fullscreen map is open. On a server the clock keeps running.

Day and night do not cause ambient-temperature survival penalties. Temperature-free survival and shelter

Weather

  1. The weather cycle takes 30 minutes. Each step lasts 3 minutes.
  2. The order is clear, cloudy, rain, cloudy, partly cloudy, foggy, cloudy, rainstorm, thunderstorm, cloudy. Then it starts again.
  3. Rain, cloud, mist and wind blend over about 15 seconds when the step changes, so there is no sudden switch.

Each world starts at a different point in the cycle. The whole world shares one weather pattern, so rain falls over deserts too. There is no snowfall. To see the current step, press Esc, choose Settings and open Gameplay > World: the Weather row reads, for example, Auto / rain. Automatic weather

  • Clear: a cloudless sky. Partly cloudy: scattered clouds. Cloudy: grey overcast. None of them rain.
  • Rain: steady rain and a light breeze.
  • Rainstorm: heavy rain and strong wind, with no lightning.
  • Thunderstorm: the heaviest rain, the strongest wind, and lightning with thunder.
  • Foggy: thick mist that cuts visibility, with no rain.
  • Rain stops at the first solid or liquid block, so a roof you build keeps the rain off you.
  • Under a roof, rain is heard as a softer patter on the roof.
  • Overcast and rain darken the sky, and rain thickens the haze.
  • In a thunderstorm, lightning lights up the sky and land about every 18 seconds, and thunder follows one to three seconds later. Lightning does not damage you or set anything on fire.
  • Cloud banks begin at 1,200, 1,800 and 2,500 metres above world zero.
  • Rain and its sound fade as you climb through the lowest cloud bank and stop by 1,600 metres. Flying above the clouds does not stop rain in the world below.
  • Weather never hurts you. Rain, storms and fog have no health, food, water or temperature penalty.
  • The music leans towards songs that suit the time of day, rain, storms and fog.

Wind strength changes with the weather, from about 2.8 m/s in clear weather to 8.5 m/s in a thunderstorm, so sailing is affected too. Sailing: wind, speed and tacking

Hold the time or weather in creative

  1. Press Esc, choose Settings, then open Gameplay > World.
  2. On the Time of day row, click < or > to step through Cycle, Dawn, Day, Dusk and Night. Cycle goes back to the normal day.
  3. On the Weather row, step through Auto, Clear, Partly cloudy, Cloudy, Rain, Rainstorm, Thunderstorm and Foggy. Auto goes back to the normal pattern.
Key or actionWhat it does
CycleNormal day and night.
Dawn, Day, Dusk, NightHold the sun at sunrise, midday or sunset, or hold the moon at midnight.
AutoFollow the normal weather pattern.
Clear, Partly cloudy, CloudyDry skies with no cloud, scattered cloud or overcast.
Rain, RainstormSteady rain, or heavy rain without lightning.
ThunderstormHeavy rain with lightning and thunder.
FoggyDry, low-visibility mist.

You can also pick a row with the Up / Down arrow keys and change it with Left / Right or Enter; right-click a row to step it back. Both lists wrap round. Reset page sets Time of day back to Cycle and Weather and Season back to Auto.

A held time or weather is saved with the world and stays in force if you switch to survival with F4. In survival the rows only show the current state; trying to change one says Time, weather, and season controls are read-only in survival. Time, weather and season controls (creative)

On a server, everyone shares the server's time, weather and season. Changes in this tab do not reach the server and are replaced within a few seconds.

Planned, not in the game yet

Planned, not in the game. Planned: darker nights, and regional weather where different parts of a world get different weather. Until these ship, the day length and weather pattern above are the same everywhere.

How this guide was checked

Re-checked against the game source at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026: day length, start time and sun path (environment.rs, game.rs, frame.rs), the night sky (shader.wgsl), farm animals resting at night (entities), beds and Home rest leaving the clock alone (furniture/resting.rs, home.rs), the weather order, step length and blending, the rain, cloud, fog and wind of each weather, lightning and thunder timing (environment.rs), rain stopping at blocks and at the cloud ceiling (precipitation.rs), roof rain and wildlife sounds (ambience.rs), sailing wind (sailing.rs), the clock pausing in menus (game.rs), the shared server clock (session.rs, server host, net bridge) and the Gameplay > World rows (settings.rs, ui.rs, music_settings.rs, settings_search.rs). The cloud heights still match the native before/after captures and automated altitude tests recorded at Voxelgame 61a4257 on 15 October 2026; those captures were not repeated.
